Shorty
SHOR-tee
noun (Gen X slang)
From short + -y; long an American nickname for a short man or a small child. In East Coast hip-hop and street speech of the late 1980s and early 1990s shorty (later also shawty, the Atlanta pronunciation popular in the 2000s) took two new senses: a younger kid or protégé ("my little shorty"), and, most commonly, a young woman or girlfriend. Usage ranges from affectionate to dismissive depending on the speaker.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In Gen X slang a shorty is either a younger kid who tags along — "Shorty, go home, your mom’s calling" — or, more often, a young woman: "Who’s that shorty?" The word can be affectionate, but in a great deal of 1990s rap it reduced a woman to her looks and her availability. The Christian observation begins with the oldest sense. Scripture’s most famous shorty is Zacchaeus, who "sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature" (Luk 19:3) — and Jesus stopped under his tree and called him by name. God does not measure as men measure: "man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart" (1Sa 16:7). The young are not to be despised either: "Let no man despise thy youth" (1Ti 4:12); "despise not one of these little ones" (Mat 18:10). When the word is used of young women, Paul supplies the only right posture for a young man: treat "the younger as sisters, with all purity" (1Ti 5:2). That is the test. If a boy calls a girl shorty the way he would speak of his own sister — with warmth and protection — little harm is done. If he uses it the way the songs did, to size her up, he is looking on the outward appearance and forgetting she bears God’s image. A father can tell his son: there are no "shorties" in God’s eyes — only image-bearers, and every young woman is somebody’s daughter and maybe someone’s future wife.

Webster 1828 Definition

Hip-hop slang (late 1980s–1990s, East Coast; later shawty) for a younger kid or, chiefly, a young woman; Scripture measures by the heart, not the stature (1Sa 16:7), and tells young men to treat young women as sisters, with all purity (1Ti 5:2).

SHORTY, n. (Gen X slang, late 1980s–1990s, East Coast hip-hop and street speech) A young woman or girlfriend; also a younger kid, a protégé. "Who’s that shorty by the lockers?"

Variant shawty (Atlanta, 2000s). Older sense: a nickname for a short person.

Tone ranges from affectionate (little brother, little sister) to appraising and dismissive (a girl sized up by looks).

Webster 1828: SHORT, a. [Latin curtus.] 1. Not long; not having great length or extension; as a short distance; a short ferry; a short flight; a short piece of timber. …

Decode for parents: ask how your son means it; teach him to speak of young women as sisters, with all purity (1Ti 5:2).

Key Scripture

Luk 19:3 — "And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature."

1Sa 16:7 — "But the LORD said unto Samuel, Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature; because I have refused him: for the LORD seeth not as man seeth; for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart."

1Ti 4:12 — "Let no man despise thy youth; but be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in spirit, in faith, in purity."

1Ti 5:2 — "The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity."

Mat 18:10 — "Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven."

Modern Corruption

Shorty can be warm, but in much hip-hop it sized up young women by looks and availability; Scripture measures by the heart and commands young men to treat young women as sisters, with all purity.

expand to see more

Sizing up. The trouble with shorty was never the height joke; it was the eye behind it. In many 1990s songs a shorty was a girl appraised and pursued, rarely a person known. That is the outward-appearance looking that God refused when Samuel admired Eliab (1Sa 16:7). A boy trained by the music to evaluate girls will find it hard to honor a wife. Paul’s rule — the younger as sisters, with all purity (1Ti 5:2) — turns the appraising eye into a protecting one.

The little ones. The older, kinder sense of the word survives in neighborhoods where a big kid looks out for his shorty. That instinct is good, and Jesus blesses it: despise not one of these little ones (Mat 18:10). Zacchaeus was the shorty of Jericho, mocked and pushed aside by the crowd, and he was the one Jesus went home with (Luk 19:3). God has a long record of choosing the overlooked.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

English short → nickname shorty (a small man, a child) → late-1980s East Coast hip-hop shorty (young woman; younger kid) → Atlanta shawty; Scripture: the LORD looketh on the heart (1Sa 16:7).
